title: Narrow task scope excludes a complete medication plan
diagnosis: The medication list exists and is correctly attributed to Elena. Owens has only a nausea/adherence service grant. Reviews explicitly exclude the full list and medication-start/dose instructions. The answer model receives ten other records and marks every one unrelated. There is no patient-subject hold at this checkpoint; the compartment hold count does not explain this omission.

title: Historical consent is rendered alongside current revocation
diagnosis: The output includes revoked family access and removal of Linda, but also renders earlier time/location consent as current. The answer model itself labels old permission statements current. Current-policy state and historical statements are not reliably distinguished.

title: Wrong recipient revoked; patient hold also blocks scheduling facts
diagnosis: Turn 138 requests revocation of the mother. The published operations instead revoke two scheduling grants whose participant is scheduler_jules. A separate unresolved erasure hold on Elena starts at turn 154. Either issue matters; removing the hold alone does not restore the incorrectly revoked grants.

title: Subject-wide hold blocks retained allergy and calendar facts
diagnosis: Elena has an active ownership grant. Her unresolved turn-154 erasure control holds the entire subject, including allergy and schedule information unrelated to the requested deletion. No evidence reaches an answer model.

title: Subject hold and narrow pharmacy grant
diagnosis: The full medication plan is stored. Klein has a metoprolol-only clarification grant; other medication fields are explicitly excluded by reviews. A turn-73 patient-subject control hold additionally blocks Marcus facts. Two unrelated records reach the answer model and both are labeled unrelated.

title: Current revocation facts withheld; old consent statement answered
diagnosis: A patient-subject hold already exists. The desk receives an older statement about updating Nina while consent remains active, rather than the current revocation and routing instructions. The final answer repeats the old conditional permission.

title: Patient hold blocks procedure logistics; preparation scope also needs review
diagnosis: Marcus has been held since turn 73. Terry has scheduling/arrival grants, but the packet contains only family/driver statements. The complete procedure/preparation requirements never reach the answer model; whether all preparation belongs to the accepted scheduling service is a separate scope question.

title: Subject hold blocks owned follow-up plan
diagnosis: Marcus owns his information, but unresolved patient control events at turns 73 and 127 hold it. The full follow-up recap is in the available prefix; the query receives an empty packet.

title: Subject hold blocks owned discharge plan
diagnosis: Active ownership does not bypass unresolved patient-subject holds. The discharge medication and follow-up instructions exist in the source prefix, but the query receives an empty packet.

title: Patient hold plus no matching return-precautions grant
diagnosis: Jamison has several accepted assessment/medication services. The patient-subject hold prevents Marcus evidence from being released. The host also classifies the requested return-precautions category outside the retained approved scopes and returns refuse. A nursing title is not a permission receipt.

title: Failed deletion leaves unrelated current contacts held
diagnosis: Failed erasure controls remain unresolved; the latest ownership grant remains active. The query receives no retained current-contact evidence. This is not evidence that all current contacts were actually erased.

title: Accumulated subject holds block late current-state plan
diagnosis: Marcus retains an active ownership grant but multiple unresolved patient controls. Only an unrelated record reaches the answer model. Large pending-review counts coexist with holds and do not identify a unique causal pair.

title: Recognized scheduling acceptance disappears during repair
diagnosis: Turn 44 initially recognizes service acceptance for scheduler_tess but references a grant belonging to somebody else. Validation demands a recipient-specific grant. The repair calls the same utterance mere attendance confirmation and publishes no scheduling grant for Tess. At the checkpoint Tess has only ownership of Tess information; Jonah appointment facts are stored but inaccessible.

title: Narrow clinical scope and unsupported answer
diagnosis: The objective staging facts are stored. Monroe has a symptom/medication-review grant, and reviews exclude lab/staging results. The answer model nevertheless claims that symptoms substantiate an objective staging summary. Valid citation IDs did not prove that cited text answered the question.

title: Narrow scope and unsupported monitoring answer
diagnosis: The monitoring date and panels are stored. Reviews exclude them as outside symptom/medication review. The answer model cites symptom history as support for the requested monitoring items and timing.

title: Unresolved family revocation holds the patient; scheduling scope narrow
diagnosis: Tess has a video-follow-up scheduling grant, while failed family revocation controls hold all Jonah information. The packet is empty. This does not show that the calendar recap failed extraction.

title: Unresolved family revocation blocks owner contact query
diagnosis: Jonah has an active ownership grant but unresolved controls from revoking family access. The broad hold also blocks the patient reading the surviving current-contact plan. The query packet is empty.

title: Subject hold and narrow medication-service scope
diagnosis: The OTC guidance is in the source prefix and retained memory. Keane has missed-dose/adherence services, not an unrestricted medication grant; the subject hold is an additional blocker. The query packet is empty.

title: Ordinary question causes a subject-wide control hold
diagnosis: Both turn-39 control attempts fail an identifier enum. The utterance asks whether to continue vitamins/iron. The resulting Nadia hold persists. The exact BP recap is correctly attributed and explicitly bound to active ownership, but the hold blocks release; no answer-generation call is made.

title: Same question-induced hold blocks pain list
diagnosis: The current pain list is in the available prefix. Nadia retains ownership, but the turn-39 hold blocks all Nadia facts. The query packet is empty.

title: Approved calendar facts blocked by patient hold
diagnosis: The final appointment dates are stored and the scheduler reviews say bound. Nadia is nevertheless held. The only released records describe the scheduler actions, not the final dates. The answer model labels those fragments sufficient and outputs an incomplete calendar.

title: Same hold blocks current temporary contact plan
diagnosis: The patient owner has no released packet because the Nadia subject remains held. A later pending queue does not undo the earlier hold.

title: Approved nurse task still blocked by patient hold
diagnosis: Patel has an accepted same-day-call service covering blood pressure, symptoms and call criteria. The desired trigger recap exists, but the Nadia hold blocks it. The single retrieved check-in record does not support the request.

title: Patient hold and front-desk scope mismatch
diagnosis: Gwen has a narrow early intake grant. The Nadia hold blocks current patient facts, leaving only staff chart-confusion statements. Location/arrival scope needs to be established by task authority, independently of clearing the hold.

title: Home-recovery service exists but patient remains held
diagnosis: Franklin has an accepted home-recovery-list service. The listed items are in the prefix, but the patient-subject hold prevents their release. The packet is empty.

title: New contact recap blocked after deletion
diagnosis: The current callback recap is separate from the requested old backup details. Nadia ownership remains active, but her pre-existing turn-39 hold blocks the current recap too. The packet is empty.

title: Subject hold and narrow pharmacy-scope classification
diagnosis: The current home list exists. Lin has a medication-safety/interaction grant, and Nadia remains held. The host absence classification yields refuse; no evidence is supplied to an answer generator.

title: Current calendar bound but held; staff fragments answered
diagnosis: The final recap is correctly stored and a scheduler review says bound. The patient hold blocks release. Old self-attributed scheduling statements remain accessible and the model renders these as the final calendar.

title: Nurse never receives a matching patient medication grant
diagnosis: The recap is correctly attributed to Lila and approved for Lila ownership. Ross instead has Ross ownership and a service about Aaron appointment times. No Lila medication grant is present. The host returns refuse. Clearing a control hold would not create the missing task authority.

title: Speaker misattribution makes an old medication card look current
diagnosis: The old medication recap is incorrectly attributed to pharmacist_imani and bound under pharmacist ownership. The updated card including melatonin is attributed to Lila; Imani has no matching Lila grant. Only the old card reaches the answer model, which calls it current.

title: Failed deletion control holds current direct contact plan
diagnosis: Lila retains ownership, but the failed turn-131 deletion control holds all Lila information. The new direct-contact recap does not reach an answer model.

title: Missing care-task grant plus patient control hold
diagnosis: The stable return-now criteria appear earlier in the prefix. Vega has only ownership of Vega information, not a matching Lila care-service grant. Lila also has a patient-subject hold. The query packet is empty. A successful repair needs both appropriate task authority and usable evidence.

title: Wrong information subject in self-service authority
diagnosis: The red-flag facts are correctly attributed to Maya. Priya has only Priya ownership and a self-service grant about Priya. Neither authorizes Maya facts. A nurse-origin hold is not an explanation for granting access to Maya. The query packet is empty.

title: Pharmacist has no patient-task authority
diagnosis: The medication plan is stored with Maya as subject. Omar has only Omar ownership; no Maya grant is present. The raw-stream contract supplies no role-based read permission. An operational task receipt is needed if this benchmark expectation is to be served safely.

title: Historical recovery suspends valid ownership; answer also omits evidence
diagnosis: The turn-54 backup and isolated reproduction establish that historical no-op recovery suspended legitimate ownership/current grants. Full treatment instructions were then excluded under narrow remaining grants. The earlier vitamin/levothyroxine history was actually in the packet at index 7, but the successful answer response labeled it unrelated. See the earlier utility-diagnosis report for the exact transition reproduction.

title: Proposal context lost; appointment assigned to scheduler
diagnosis: The full Thursday offer is classified context/question and becomes no fact. Acceptance retains only Thursday at 8:10. The March 11 booking is attributed to scheduler_jules, not Elena, so no Elena-family grant review is generated. Linda has an active time/location grant. Three of five required items are covered.

title: Cancellation incorrectly excluded from logistics scope
diagnosis: Both cancellation facts are stored with Elena as subject. The Linda review excludes one because cancellation status is not time or location, and excludes the complete recap because it contains date and arrival time. The final answer has the Friday slot but omits cancellation of Monday. This is an explicit negative review, not an outstanding approval.

title: Operational contact excluded; patient hold adds another barrier
diagnosis: The new number, generic-message rule and portal preference are stored. Casey has accepted imaging/emergency/symptom services, but reviews exclude contact routing as unrelated. A patient-subject hold also starts at turn 104. Only two self-attributed staff-action records reach the answer model; it presents these as responsive callback instructions. This combines scope interpretation, a control failure and answer entailment failure.

title: Existing damaged ownership plus a newer subject hold
diagnosis: The complete updated follow-up facts are stored with Elena as subject. Ownership remains suspended from historical recovery. A turn-104 Understood acknowledgment fails a grant lookup and leaves a patient-subject hold. At turn 134 the exact recorded query packet is empty; the host returns no_memory without an answer-generation call. There are 397 pending pairs overall, but that count does not show which exact missing fact would be restored by queue draining.
